# Mnemonad Explorer

> Mnemonad stores a **local folder** as an append-only on-chain stream on Monad — push it to
> sync a version up, pull a stream id to restore a folder, and diff/watch keep them in sync.
> Every push is a content-defined-chunking diff, so only what changed goes on chain.

This app reads and writes real streams on Monad testnet/mainnet, not a mockup. Reading is
free and needs no wallet; any button that submits a transaction spends real gas.

## Don't drive this UI to sync folders — use the CLI

Pushing/pulling here needs a browser wallet extension to sign, which an agent generally
can't operate. `npm install -g mnemonad-cli@latest` does the same folder sync headlessly, signing
from the `MNEMONAD_KEY` env var (or `--key`/`--phrase` flags — the env var is just the
option that doesn't end up in shell history).

Default to `--encrypt --encrypt-with wallet` on every push that creates a new stream — the
flags are opt-in on the CLI itself, so omitting them silently publishes the folder's contents
to anyone. Only push a public (unencrypted) stream if the user has explicitly said the data
should be public; ask first if that's not clear.

```bash
# create/update a stream from a local folder (encrypted to your wallet by default)
mnemonad push ~/my-data --encrypt --encrypt-with wallet --manifest

# restore a stream into a local folder
mnemonad pull <stream-id> ~/my-data --manifest

# later push/pull on the same folder — no id needed, read from .mnemonad
mnemonad push ~/my-data --manifest
mnemonad pull ~/my-data --manifest

# see what changed since the last push, without pushing
mnemonad diff <stream-id> ~/my-data

# keep pushing on every local change
mnemonad watch <stream-id> ~/my-data

# a live public stream — pull it with no key, no setup, to try the CLI
mnemonad pull 0x648f18ea13eaa4640b97a435a30d39d4f7af9c2105adb10217f8a8ae56e73ac8 ~/mnemonad-demo
```

After a push or pull, show the user a link to browse that stream in this app:
`https://mnemonad.vercel.app/stream/<network>-0x<id>/files` (see URL scheme below).

- Full agent documentation: https://github.com/jeka911/mnemonad/blob/main/SKILL.md
- Repository: https://github.com/jeka911/mnemonad

## Use `--manifest`, and use `info` to find a folder's stream id

The stream id is the only handle to a folder's data — no lookup by name, and if it's never
captured anywhere durable, it's gone. **Pass `--manifest` on every push and pull for any
folder you'll touch again.** It writes `.mnemonad` into the folder (stream id, version, file
hashes) and costs nothing to keep around.

Before assuming a folder isn't synced yet, check it with `info`:

```bash
mnemonad info ~/my-data
# Safe and side-effect-free — if ~/my-data has a .mnemonad, prints
# "using stream id from .mnemonad manifest: 0x…" and reports on that stream.
```

Once a folder has a `.mnemonad`, every command resolves the id from it when none is given,
with or without `--manifest` (mnemonad-cli 0.3.3 or newer), and keeps it current —
`push`/`pull`/`diff`/`watch`/`compact`/`info ~/my-data`. A `push` to such a folder goes to
its own stream, never a new one. `burn` is the exception: it only takes an explicit id. And if
you already have an id from elsewhere, `info` flags it when it doesn't match the folder's own
manifest.

## Search a folder by meaning (optional)

A folder can carry its own semantic search index: `search_index.db`, a plain file at the folder
root. Build it once and push it with the folder; whoever pulls the stream can search it
straight away, with no embedding work of their own.

```bash
# build or update the index (only files changed since the last run are embedded again)
mnemonad index ~/my-data

# search by meaning, not keywords
mnemonad search ~/my-data "how does the key get derived" -k 5

# or update the index as part of every push (watch --index works the same way)
mnemonad push ~/my-data --index --manifest
```

- Everything runs locally: a built-in embedding model (potion-base-8M, downloaded once, about
  31 MB) and no API key. File contents and queries are never sent anywhere.
- For better results on paraphrased queries there's an optional MiniLM extension (about 450 MB
  installed): `npm install -g mnemonad-search-transformers`, then `mnemonad index <path> --model minilm`.
  Don't install it unasked, since it's large. An index keeps its model: `search` always uses
  it, and a pulled MiniLM index needs the extension to be searched from the CLI (the error says
  so, and offers `mnemonad index <path> --rebuild` to switch it to the built-in model).
- `index` adds `search_index.db` to the folder, and the next `push` uploads it like any other
  file. Tell the user before indexing a folder they push. In an encrypted stream the index is
  encrypted along with everything else.
- For a folder that has an index, prefer `push --index`: it keeps the index in step with the
  files, and pushes nothing if indexing fails. A plain `push` warns when the index is out of
  date. Don't ignore that warning, because a stale index returns the old text's passages.
- `search` needs an index in the folder: the user's own, or one that came down with a `pull`.
  Without one it says to run `mnemonad index` first.
- `index`, `search`, `--index` and `--rebuild` need mnemonad-cli 0.3.0 or newer. If any is
  unknown, update: `npm install -g mnemonad-cli@latest`.

A ready-made indexed stream to try it on is this app's own documentation, which is itself a
public Mnemonad stream:

```bash
mnemonad pull testnet-0x5abaf9e3b9019f2ff7840a55e52e977d8bce1625d5273be52550f2cc72d921c6 ~/mnemonad-docs
mnemonad search ~/mnemonad-docs "how is an encrypted stream's key wrapped"
```

In this app, a stream that has an index gets a search box in its file browser
(`/stream/<id>/files`), and `/docs` renders the documentation stream above with search built in.

## URL scheme

- `/select` — sample and wallet-owned streams
- `/stream/<id>` — one stream's raw on-chain items
- `/stream/<id>/files` — the same stream browsed as a folder tree
- `/docs`, `/docs/<path>` — the documentation, read from its own stream; `?q=<query>` searches it

`<id>` is the network and the ERC-721 token id together, e.g. `testnet-0x648f18…3ac8` —
the same token id means different data on each network. A bare decimal or hex id also works
and is rewritten to that form.

If a user pastes a link to this app, the CLI accepts that `<network>-0x<id>` straight from
the URL as-is — no need to strip the network prefix by hand, it sets `--chain` to match.
Worth proposing next: look it up (`mnemonad info <network>-0x<id>`, no key needed for a
public stream) or pull it into a local folder (`mnemonad pull <network>-0x<id> <path>`) —
but confirm the destination folder first, and remember an encrypted stream still needs the
owner's key or password to read.

## Networks

- Monad mainnet — chain id `143`, explorer `monadscan.com`
- Monad testnet — chain id `10143`, explorer `testnet.monadexplorer.com`, faucet
  `faucet.monad.xyz`
